top.line: London to start, the US to sell, Bermuda to carry the risk
top.para: The insurer for agent behaviour policies does three jobs and can have three homes: a managing agent in London, distribution into the US and EU, its own balance sheet in Bermuda, capital from the Gulf. About £4.35 million to start; then capital that follows from the limits sold.

in-short.line: Eight lines from the three jobs to the capital
in-short.para: Three jobs, three homes; start in London; sell through US surplus lines; the EU by one registration, second; carry the risk in Bermuda; raise capital in the Gulf; £4.35 million to start; then £4.8 million to £9.6 million for 2,000 agents.

question.line: A managing agent, distribution and a balance sheet differ
question.para: Pricing and selling needs a distribution licence and a carrier's capital; carrying risk needs an insurer's licence and capital against a bad year; distribution needs licences where the customers are. Each is regulated differently in each place, so one company can have three homes.

london.line: Start as a managing agent and coverholder in London
london.para: Two of today's AI agent covers are written by Lloyd's coverholders. FCA authorisation takes up to nine months, or the appointed representative route is faster; an intermediary's capital is the higher of £5,000 or 2.5% of income. The PRA has a mobilisation regime for new insurers.

us.line: Reach the US through surplus lines
us.para: Surplus lines cover risks with no filed form or rate; the market wrote $143.3 billion in 2025, and Harbor's agent cover is issued there. A US managing agent needs state producer licences and a bond of $100,000 to $500,000. A provider's own captive starts at $250,000 in Vermont.

eu.line: The EU second: one registration, a cautious supervisor
eu.para: An intermediary registered in one member state works across the EU; software becomes a product on 9 December 2026. EIOPA wrote in June 2026 of weak oversight of MGAs and of reliance on non-EU capacity. A written, deterministic policy should answer those concerns.

bermuda.line: Carry the risk in Bermuda when the record allows
bermuda.para: A Class 3A small commercial insurer has a $1 million floor; there is an innovative class and a sandbox that cyber insurers have used; the Bermuda Stock Exchange lists over 93% of insurance-linked securities, including cyber catastrophe bonds. The UK is the alternative.

gulf.line: The Gulf as a source of capital before a market
gulf.para: Saudi insurers need SAR 300 million paid up; the ADGM's captive rules started at $150,000 and its regulator proposes holding 120% of its capital requirement. DIFC figures were not verified. The region's funds suit the balance-sheet stage.

money.line: About £4.35 million to start; then capital from limits
money.para: Two years as a managing agent: eight then fifteen people and running costs, £4.35 million. To carry the risk, limits times the share one shared failure could hit, half reinsured, plus 20%: £4.8 to £9.6 million for 2,000 agents, £24 to £48 million for 10,000.

limits.line: Not advice; my assumptions; thinner Gulf data
limits.para: Not legal, tax or regulatory advice; the model's inputs are assumptions; currencies are approximate; the Middle East figures are thinner; fronting fees and tax are left out for lack of reliable figures or relevance to a start-up.

sources.line: The third memo, a research agent, and capital.py
sources.para: From Dinis's memo of 28 October 2026, with the routes and the estimate as his opinion; every source fetched that day or marked secondary; the model and its data file are in the repository.
